## Login

### Skip the login screen after the disk unlock {#gdm-autologin}

One password at boot (LUKS), then straight to the desktop. The lock screen still asks

- **Handleiding:** [GDM Autologin]({{< relref "/docs/security/autologin" >}})
- **Alleen op:** het GNOME-bureaublad
- **Bron:** [de regel](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3405-L3407) · [`on_autologin`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1774-L1788) · [`off_autologin`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1791-L1803)

**Aanzetten**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Turn on GDM autologin for your-username (the old file is kept as custom.conf.zephyrus-setup.bak)
[ -e /etc/gdm/custom.conf.zephyrus-setup.bak ] || cp -a /etc/gdm/custom.conf /etc/gdm/custom.conf.zephyrus-setup.bak
# prepared in your cache folder by this setup: root installs it only while its SHA-256 still matches
echo '525225f730e6836251907ec31876d92d139c6376f7bacc6e87a2fe5d37ac0d37  /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/gdm-custom.conf' | sha256sum -c --quiet -
install -m 644 -o root -g root /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/gdm-custom.conf /etc/gdm/custom.conf
grep -q '^AutomaticLogin=your-username$' /etc/gdm/custom.conf || { cp -a /etc/gdm/custom.conf.zephyrus-setup.bak /etc/gdm/custom.conf; echo 'The GDM config check failed, the old file is back'; exit 1; }
```

De wijziging, als diff:

```diff
--- /etc/gdm/custom.conf
+++ /etc/gdm/custom.conf
@@ -1,6 +1,8 @@
 # GDM configuration storage
 
 [daemon]
+AutomaticLoginEnable=True
+AutomaticLogin=your-username
 
 [security]
```

- Anyone who can unlock the disk lands in your session. The lock screen still asks for your password.
- Herstart nodig: GDM autologin.

**Uitzetten (het terugdraaien)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Put the GDM config back as it was before
cp -a /etc/gdm/custom.conf.zephyrus-setup.bak /etc/gdm/custom.conf
rm -f /etc/gdm/custom.conf.zephyrus-setup.bak
```

De wijziging, als diff:

```diff
--- /etc/gdm/custom.conf
+++ /etc/gdm/custom.conf
@@ -1,8 +1,6 @@
 # GDM configuration storage
 
 [daemon]
-AutomaticLoginEnable=True
-AutomaticLogin=your-username
 
 [security]
```

- Herstart nodig: turning autologin off.

## Hardware keys

### YubiKey tools {#yubikey-tools}

pam-u2f, the smart card daemon and Yubico Authenticator

- **Handleiding:** [YubiKey 5C NFC]({{< relref "/docs/security/yubikey" >}})
- **Label:** `Advanced`
- **Bron:** [de regel](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3408-L3410) · [`on_yubikey`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1913-L1916) · [`off_yubikey`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1919-L1923) · [`yubikey_off_blocker`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L1926-L1932)

**Aanzetten**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Install packages from the repositories
pacman -S --needed --noconfirm --noprogressbar pam-u2f ccid pcsclite

# Start the smart card daemon now and at boot
systemctl enable --now pcscd.socket

# --- As you, from Flathub ---

# Install from Flathub
flatpak install -y flathub com.yubico.yubioath
```

**Uitzetten (het terugdraaien)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Stop the smart card daemon
systemctl disable --now pcscd.socket || true

# Remove packages, one at a time (one that something else still needs is kept)
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar pam-u2f
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar ccid

# --- As you, from Flathub ---

# Remove Flatpaks
flatpak uninstall -y com.yubico.yubioath
```

- pcsclite stays: other smart card tools use it.

### Register your YubiKey {#yubikey-key}

Plug it in and touch it when it blinks. It is saved for your account and nothing else changes

- **Handleiding:** [YubiKey 5C NFC]({{< relref "/docs/security/yubikey" >}})
- **Vereist:** [YubiKey tools](#yubikey-tools)
- **Label:** `Advanced`
- **Bron:** [de regel](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3411-L3414) · [`on_yubikey_key`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L2054-L2055) · [`off_yubikey_key`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L2058-L2063)

Aanvinken vinkt ook aan wat het nodig heeft.

**Aanzetten**

```bash
# --- As you ---

# Register your YubiKey: plug it in, and touch it when it blinks
umask 077; mkdir -p "$(dirname /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/yubikey-registration)"; rm -f /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/yubikey-registration
read -r -p 'Plug in your YubiKey, then press Enter. ' _
echo "Touch the key when it blinks. If it asks for a PIN, that is the PIN of the key itself."
pamu2fcfg -n > /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/yubikey-registration || { code=$?; rm -f /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/yubikey-registration; exit "$code"; }

# Save the registration of your YubiKey in ~/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys
# quicksetup.py does this itself (save_registration), and it amounts to:
umask 077
mkdir -p /home/your-username/.config/Yubico
# a first key adds the line 'your-username:<registration>' to /home/your-username/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys; a spare adds ':<registration>' to the end of your line there
# the file pamu2fcfg wrote in the step above is deleted either way: rm -f /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/yubikey-registration
```

**Uitzetten (het terugdraaien)**

```bash
# --- As you ---

# Forget the registered keys (the file is kept as u2f_keys.zephyrus-setup.bak)
mv -f /home/your-username/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys /home/your-username/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys.zephyrus-setup.bak
```

- The keys themselves are not touched. Registering again takes a few seconds.

### Register a spare YubiKey {#yubikey-spare}

A second key for the same account, for the day the first one is lost. Optional

- **Handleiding:** [YubiKey 5C NFC]({{< relref "/docs/security/yubikey" >}})
- **Vereist:** [Register your YubiKey](#yubikey-key)
- **Label:** `Advanced`
- **Bron:** [de regel](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3415-L3418) · [`on_yubikey_spare`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L2073-L2074) · [`off_yubikey_spare`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L2077-L2087)

Aanvinken vinkt ook aan wat het nodig heeft.

**Aanzetten**

```bash
# --- As you ---

# Register your spare YubiKey: plug it in, and touch it when it blinks
umask 077; mkdir -p "$(dirname /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/yubikey-registration)"; rm -f /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/yubikey-registration
read -r -p 'Take the first key out and plug in the spare one, then press Enter. ' _
echo "Touch the key when it blinks. If it asks for a PIN, that is the PIN of the key itself."
pamu2fcfg -n > /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/yubikey-registration || { code=$?; rm -f /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/yubikey-registration; exit "$code"; }

# Save the registration of your spare YubiKey in ~/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys
# quicksetup.py does this itself (save_registration), and it amounts to:
umask 077
mkdir -p /home/your-username/.config/Yubico
# a first key adds the line 'your-username:<registration>' to /home/your-username/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys; a spare adds ':<registration>' to the end of your line there
# the file pamu2fcfg wrote in the step above is deleted either way: rm -f /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/yubikey-registration
```

**Uitzetten (het terugdraaien)**

```bash
# --- As you ---

# Forget the spare key (the first registered key stays)
# quicksetup.py does this itself (keep_first): your line in the key file keeps its first registration and loses the rest,
# the file stays readable by you only (mode 600): /home/your-username/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys
sed -E -i 's/^(your-username:[^:]*).*$/\1/' /home/your-username/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys
```

### YubiKey for sudo and the lock screen {#yubikey-pam}

A touch replaces typing the password, also in the graphical sudo prompt. Without the key the password still works

- **Handleiding:** [YubiKey 5C NFC]({{< relref "/docs/security/yubikey" >}})
- **Vereist:** [Register your YubiKey](#yubikey-key)
- **Label:** `Advanced`
- **Bron:** [de regel](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3419-L3425) · [`on_yubikey_pam`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L2108-L2129) · [`off_yubikey_pam`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L2132-L2155)

Aanvinken vinkt ook aan wat het nodig heeft.

**Aanzetten**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Put the YubiKey line first in /etc/pam.d/sudo (the old file is kept as sudo.zephyrus-setup.bak)
[ -e /usr/lib/security/pam_u2f.so ] || { echo 'pam_u2f.so is not installed, so PAM would have nothing to call'; exit 1; }
[ -e /etc/pam.d/sudo.zephyrus-setup.bak ] || cp -a /etc/pam.d/sudo /etc/pam.d/sudo.zephyrus-setup.bak
# prepared in your cache folder by this setup: root installs it only while its SHA-256 still matches
echo '5c08ed1665c85342ddd5acd90acdd1dadd47757c05090c9022149f10ba5b07be  /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/pam-sudo' | sha256sum -c --quiet -
install -m 644 -o root -g root /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/pam-sudo /etc/pam.d/sudo
grep -Eq '^auth[[:space:]]+sufficient[[:space:]]+pam_u2f\.so' /etc/pam.d/sudo || { cp -a /etc/pam.d/sudo.zephyrus-setup.bak /etc/pam.d/sudo; echo 'The PAM check failed, the old file is back'; exit 1; }

# Put the YubiKey line first in /etc/pam.d/polkit-1 (a copy of the file the package ships, in /etc/pam.d)
[ -e /usr/lib/security/pam_u2f.so ] || { echo 'pam_u2f.so is not installed, so PAM would have nothing to call'; exit 1; }
# prepared in your cache folder by this setup: root installs it only while its SHA-256 still matches
echo '916c5bf4d4429efa9f3c51f2628de774bfefc26c6d39ff45cfc71eae4c762d74  /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/pam-polkit-1' | sha256sum -c --quiet -
install -m 644 -o root -g root /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/pam-polkit-1 /etc/pam.d/polkit-1
grep -Eq '^auth[[:space:]]+sufficient[[:space:]]+pam_u2f\.so' /etc/pam.d/polkit-1 || { rm -f /etc/pam.d/polkit-1; echo 'The PAM check failed, the old file is back'; exit 1; }

# Put the YubiKey line first in /etc/pam.d/gdm-password (the old file is kept as gdm-password.zephyrus-setup.bak)
[ -e /usr/lib/security/pam_u2f.so ] || { echo 'pam_u2f.so is not installed, so PAM would have nothing to call'; exit 1; }
[ -e /etc/pam.d/gdm-password.zephyrus-setup.bak ] || cp -a /etc/pam.d/gdm-password /etc/pam.d/gdm-password.zephyrus-setup.bak
# prepared in your cache folder by this setup: root installs it only while its SHA-256 still matches
echo 'ae0f3732c4aca611ba6d742ebf68c6aa280a0941cb925460d136f9dc5d15f57d  /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/pam-gdm-password' | sha256sum -c --quiet -
install -m 644 -o root -g root /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/pam-gdm-password /etc/pam.d/gdm-password
grep -Eq '^auth[[:space:]]+sufficient[[:space:]]+pam_u2f\.so' /etc/pam.d/gdm-password || { cp -a /etc/pam.d/gdm-password.zephyrus-setup.bak /etc/pam.d/gdm-password; echo 'The PAM check failed, the old file is back'; exit 1; }
```

De wijziging, als diff:

```diff
--- /etc/pam.d/sudo
+++ /etc/pam.d/sudo
@@ -1,4 +1,6 @@
 #%PAM-1.0
+# Added by Zephyrus Setup: touch the YubiKey instead of typing the password
+auth       sufficient   pam_u2f.so cue
 auth		include		system-auth
 account		include		system-auth
 session		include		system-auth
```

```diff
--- /usr/lib/pam.d/polkit-1
+++ /etc/pam.d/polkit-1
@@ -1,5 +1,7 @@
 #%PAM-1.0
 
+# Added by Zephyrus Setup: touch the YubiKey instead of typing the password
+auth       sufficient   pam_u2f.so cue
 auth       include      system-auth
 account    include      system-auth
 password   include      system-auth
```

```diff
--- /etc/pam.d/gdm-password
+++ /etc/pam.d/gdm-password
@@ -1,5 +1,7 @@
 #%PAM-1.0
 
+# Added by Zephyrus Setup: touch the YubiKey instead of typing the password
+auth       sufficient   pam_u2f.so cue
 auth       include                     system-local-login
 auth       optional                    pam_gnome_keyring.so
```

- A touch of the key now replaces the password for sudo, the graphical prompt and the lock screen, so whoever holds the key can use them. Without the key plugged in, the password works as before.
- Test sudo in a second terminal before you close this one.

**Voor jou over na het aanvinken**

1. Open a second terminal and run: sudo true. Touch the key when it blinks. Keep the first terminal open until that works
2. Lock the screen with Super+L and touch the key to unlock it

**Uitzetten (het terugdraaien)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Take the YubiKey line out of /etc/pam.d/sudo
# prepared in your cache folder by this setup: root installs it only while its SHA-256 still matches
echo '7ec1c668c10e0f83d00e25f336872212fe04ce2c2563e1d661d34d28852f4649  /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/pam-sudo' | sha256sum -c --quiet -
install -m 644 -o root -g root /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/pam-sudo /etc/pam.d/sudo
rm -f /etc/pam.d/sudo.zephyrus-setup.bak

# Take the YubiKey line out of /etc/pam.d/polkit-1 by removing the copy, so the file the package ships is used again
rm -f /etc/pam.d/polkit-1 /etc/pam.d/polkit-1.zephyrus-setup.bak

# Take the YubiKey line out of /etc/pam.d/gdm-password
# prepared in your cache folder by this setup: root installs it only while its SHA-256 still matches
echo 'b4420586141757e65c9c68f0c9f0830e5e11a8daf8b71b383a115ebd59615fa8  /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/pam-gdm-password' | sha256sum -c --quiet -
install -m 644 -o root -g root /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/pam-gdm-password /etc/pam.d/gdm-password
rm -f /etc/pam.d/gdm-password.zephyrus-setup.bak
```

De wijziging, als diff:

```diff
--- /etc/pam.d/sudo
+++ /etc/pam.d/sudo
@@ -1,6 +1,4 @@
 #%PAM-1.0
-# Added by Zephyrus Setup: touch the YubiKey instead of typing the password
-auth       sufficient   pam_u2f.so cue
 auth		include		system-auth
 account		include		system-auth
 session		include		system-auth
```

```diff
--- /etc/pam.d/polkit-1
+++ /usr/lib/pam.d/polkit-1
@@ -1,7 +1,5 @@
 #%PAM-1.0
 
-# Added by Zephyrus Setup: touch the YubiKey instead of typing the password
-auth       sufficient   pam_u2f.so cue
 auth       include      system-auth
 account    include      system-auth
 password   include      system-auth
```

```diff
--- /etc/pam.d/gdm-password
+++ /etc/pam.d/gdm-password
@@ -1,7 +1,5 @@
 #%PAM-1.0
 
-# Added by Zephyrus Setup: touch the YubiKey instead of typing the password
-auth       sufficient   pam_u2f.so cue
 auth       include                     system-local-login
 auth       optional                    pam_gnome_keyring.so
```

## Secure Boot

### sbctl {#sbctl}

The tool that creates and enrolls your own Secure Boot keys

- **Handleiding:** [Secure Boot]({{< relref "/docs/cachyos/secure-boot" >}})
- **Label:** `Advanced`
- **Bron:** [de regel](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3426-L3428) · [`sbctl_off_blocker`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L2163-L2168)

**Aanzetten**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Install packages from the repositories
pacman -S --needed --noconfirm --noprogressbar sbctl
```

**Uitzetten (het terugdraaien)**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Remove packages, one at a time (one that something else still needs is kept)
pacman -Rs --noconfirm --noprogressbar sbctl
```

### Secure Boot with your own keys {#secure-boot}

Keys, firmware setup and signing the boot files: a mistake can stop the machine from booting, so it stays manual

- **Handleiding:** [Secure Boot]({{< relref "/docs/cachyos/secure-boot" >}})
- **Label:** `Advanced`
- **Bron:** [de regel](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3429-L3443)

Deze rij is een handleiding en heeft geen vinkje: de stappen blijven van jou, omdat een fout erin de machine kan laten stoppen met opstarten.

**Met de hand, om het in te richten**

1. Reboot into the ASUS UEFI (systemctl reboot --firmware-setup) and put Secure Boot in Setup Mode
2. sudo sbctl create-keys
3. sudo sbctl enroll-keys --microsoft
4. Sign the boot files: sbctl-batch-sign for systemd-boot, limine-enroll-config and limine-update for Limine
5. Enable Secure Boot in the UEFI again, then check with: sudo sbctl status

**Met de hand, om het terug te draaien**

1. Reboot into the ASUS UEFI (systemctl reboot --firmware-setup) and set Secure Boot Control to Disabled, under Security > Secure Boot. The machine boots as before
2. Optional: your own keys do no harm while Secure Boot is off. Put the firmware's default keys back under Key Management only if you want them gone
3. Optional: untick sbctl in this window to remove the tool and its pacman hook, which re-signs new kernels
